**macOS now comes as a disk image.** Open the `.dmg` and drag Cloak to
Applications, or copy it anywhere else (a USB stick, say) to run it
portably.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.2.3-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.2.3-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again).

## What's new

- **macOS disk image** instead of a zip, with the usual drag-to-Applications
  layout.
- **Installed or portable on macOS.** Installed in Applications, Cloak keeps
  its drive list and settings in `~/.cloak`. Run from any other folder, it
  keeps them in a `cloak-data` folder beside the app, as on Windows.
  Settings → Storage shows which applies.

## Known limitations

- **The macOS app has not yet been tested on a real Mac.** Treat it as a
  preview and keep a backup of anything you put in a drive.
- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- FUSE-T is not supported yet (macFUSE only).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
